trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Tag_Processor, next_tag(), get_attribute_names_with_prefix(), remove_attribute(), and get_updated_html(), all documented. The solution follows the flat attribute-edit pattern and correctly handles the documented null return shape.
Identical API usage to the reference pattern. Correct processor choice, no undocumented calls, idiomatic scan/edit/get_updated_html flow, and no _doing_it_wrong records.
Correctly used the Tag Processor for byte-preserving attribute removal across all tags. All called methods are present in the rendered docs and execution reported no API misuse.

failure_analysis: No hidden cases failed across the three trials; each passed 7/7. The rendered docs did well on the exact concepts this task required: html-tag-processor.md explains that WP_HTML_Tag_Processor is for flat, position-based attribute/class edits while WP_HTML_Processor is for structure-aware work; the Basic Usage and next_tag() sections show direct construction plus linear tag walking; the Modifying HTML attributes and remove_attribute() sections document safe attribute removal; get_attribute_names_with_prefix() documents lowercase returned names and the null case when no tag opener is matched; get_updated_html() clearly states it is the way to retrieve queued edits while preserving untouched bytes. Near-miss: get_attribute_names_with_prefix() implies case-insensitive matching through its example and spec reference, but the prose could state that the prefix comparison itself is ASCII case-insensitive and that returned lowercase names are suitable for remove_attribute().

doc_gaps.problem: The section shows case-insensitive behavior by example, but the main prose does not directly say whether the supplied prefix is compared ASCII-case-insensitively against source attribute names.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one sentence to the contract: prefix matching is ASCII-case-insensitive for HTML attribute names, and the returned names are normalized lowercase.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs do not explicitly state that returned normalized names can be passed back into mutation APIs such as remove_attribute(), which is the natural bulk-edit workflow.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that names returned by get_attribute_names_with_prefix() are valid target names for get_attribute(), set_attribute(), and remove_attribute() on the current matched tag.
